title: Martial Arts Trial Class Booking Software (2026)
description: Trial and intro-class booking for martial arts schools: 10 tools compared on online booking, lead forms, automated follow-up, texting costs and price.
h1: Martial arts trial class booking software
keyword: martial arts trial class booking software
body:
Most new students at a martial arts school start with a trial: one free class, an intro week, or a paid starter pack. The software question is simple. Can a parent or adult book that first class from your website or a social post at 9 p.m., get a confirmation and a reminder, and then get followed up if they don't show or don't sign up? And what does that cost on top of the software you already need for billing and belts?

This page compares what ten vendors publish about trial and intro-class booking, lead capture and follow-up. We checked each vendor's own pricing and feature pages on November 26, 2026. We haven't used these tools ourselves and we don't publish ratings. Anything a vendor doesn't publish is marked unknown. Prices are in US dollars. For booking regular classes for existing students, see BJJ class scheduling software; for yoga and Pilates style class booking, see class booking software for studios.

What trial-class software needs to do

  • A public way to book the trial. A booking page, landing page or embedded form that puts the prospect into a real class slot, not just an email to your inbox.
  • Waiver and contact details up front. So the first class doesn't start with paperwork.
  • Automatic confirmation and reminders. Email and/or text before the class.
  • Follow-up after the trial. A sequence for no-shows and for people who came but didn't join, plus a list or pipeline so nobody slips through.
  • Clear costs. Some vendors include all of this in the base plan; others sell it as a marketing add-on, and texting is often billed per message.

Black Friday offers on these pages

  • Spark Membership: 50% off for 12 months plus the 8 weeks free, for new schools only; Spark says that saves $1,592 in year one. Ends Dec 4 (pricing page, checked 2026-11-26).
  • PushPress: 30% off any PushPress product, including Grow, for your first 6 months, for new and returning gyms who sign up by December 11, 2026; can't be combined with other promotions. On Grow's $329/mo list price that works out to $230.30/mo for 6 months (our arithmetic).

Do leads and trial students count toward your bill?

On tools priced by student count, a busy trial pipeline could push you into a higher tier. Martialytics says "Leads and Inactive Students are free." Gymdesk says visitors and prospects aren't counted toward active members. Zen Planner says prospects are never charged; an active member is anyone with a membership or who "attended an event in the past month", while pay-per-session attendees are never counted, so ask how a free trial attendee is counted. PushPress lists unlimited leads on every plan. Dojo Champ and Spark have one price regardless of student count. Kicksite prices by active students and doesn't say on its pricing page whether prospects count.

How to choose

  • Want trial booking and follow-up in the base price: Gymdesk, Kicksite, Dojo Champ, Spark and MAAT all describe it without a separate marketing add-on. Gymdesk ($75 to $100) and MAAT ($49 to $59 + 1%) have the lowest published prices for a small school.
  • Lots of walk-ins and flyers: Kicksite (tablet kiosk mode and QR codes) and MatPilot (short links and QR codes) describe this directly.
  • Heavy texting: compare Kicksite's free texting and RhinoFit's "no SMS fees" against Dojo Champ ($0.03 per segment after 100 credits) and Gymdesk (usage-based). Texting to US numbers also needs carrier registration; ask each vendor how they handle it.
  • Already on PushPress or Zen Planner: lead follow-up is a paid step up (Grow $329/mo; Zen Planner Ultimate $348/mo or Engage from $249/mo), so price it against switching.
  • Just starting out: see free and low-cost martial arts software and the martial arts software hub.

faq: Which martial arts software lets prospects book a free trial class online?

Gymdesk (intro classes or trial sessions on your calendar), Kicksite (begin a trial from forms or landing pages), Dojo Champ (public intro-class booking page), MatPilot (free or paid trials tracked in the pipeline) and MAAT (single free trial classes or 7-day free trial memberships) describe this on their own pages. Spark routes trial form submissions into its CRM, and PushPress handles intro follow-up in its Grow add-on (vendor pages, checked 2026-11-26).
Is lead follow-up included or an extra cost?

Gymdesk, Kicksite, Dojo Champ, Spark and MAAT describe automated trial or lead follow-up on their main plans. PushPress sells it as Grow at $329/mo on top of Core, and Zen Planner lists automated lead follow-up on Ultimate ($348/mo) or the Engage add-on (from $249/mo) (pricing pages, checked 2026-11-26).

Kicksite advertises free unlimited texting (one-way on its pricing page, two-way on its features page). RhinoFit Standard says no email or SMS fees. Dojo Champ includes 100 SMS credits, then $0.03 per segment. Gymdesk SMS is a usage-based add-on with rates not published. Others don't state SMS costs (vendor pages, checked 2026-11-26).
Will trial students push me into a higher price tier?

Martialytics says leads are free, Gymdesk doesn't count visitors or prospects as active members, and Zen Planner never charges for prospects but counts anyone who attended an event in the past month as active (pay-per-session attendees aren't counted). Dojo Champ and Spark charge one price regardless of student count (pricing pages, checked 2026-11-26).
